text: Voice traffic, voice over IP, or you have video, video conference in video streaming. Well, as we already said, these are types of applications that require low latency. Otherwise, the quality of the service for the user is not good enough. If you have delays when you talk over Zoom or other, um, WeChat or other applications that you may use, well, you get annoyed, right? Because you start talking and the other actually is overlapping with his voice, it's a mess. So these kind of applications really need low latency, low delay. If you think about how PCF works based on contention, if WiFi nodes have got packets to transmit, well, who knows when they get chance to transmit? Okay, it's kind of random. It depends on how many nodes are there, how much traffic we have to transmit. It depends on the wireless channel conditions. There are many things that may go wrong. So the standard said, well, we need to introduce a different access scheme whenever we have traffic that needs to be transmitted with low delay. And that's why they initially specified PCF because as we said in this case, there is no randomness in access, right? Channel access. It's the access point that says, "You can transmit, you can transmit, you can transmit." So it's more deterministic. So you may wonder, okay, it's a good thing. It could help to.
